Subject: RE: Acme - MSA redline (IP indemnity carve-out)

Rachel / Karthik — see my take below and suggested redline (attached). Key points:

- We should not accept an uncapped indemnity. Instead propose: IP infringement indemnity remains excepted from the standard liability cap only to the extent of direct damages and reasonable defense costs caused by a third-party claim, and limited to a fixed sub-cap of $3,000,000.
- Preserve our right to cure: allow Redwood to obtain a license, modify the service, or otherwise remedy the alleged infringement before damages are assessed.
- Control of defense: require prompt notice and sole control of defense, but Acme may participate at its own counsel expense. We should require cooperation and access to evidence.
- Exclude consequential and punitive damages (explicitly), and exclude claims arising from customer content where the customer (Acme) provided the infringing material.

Suggested language (summary): 
"Notwithstanding Section X (Limitation of Liability), Redwood's liability for third-party claims alleging infringement of a third party's intellectual property shall be subject to a per-claim cap of $3,000,000 and limited to direct damages and reasonable costs of defense; such indemnity shall not include consequential, special, exemplary, or punitive damages. Redwood shall have the right, at its option and expense, to (a) procure for Customer the right to continue using the Service, (b) replace or modify the Service to make it non-infringing, or (c) terminate the affected Service and refund any prepaid fees covering the remainder of the term."

Rationale: this balances Acme's ask for meaningful protection (and defense cost coverage) with a commercially finite Redwood exposure. If Sales needs a clean uncapped carve-out to close, we should quantify a mitigation (e.g., additional fee, escrow, or insurance requirement).

I've attached a tracked version with inline edits (Redwood_response_redline.docx). If Acme insists on uncapped liability for IP, escalate to Legal Ops to discuss insurance/indemnity carve-out economics.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Team — quick note from Sales perspective. We need to keep the commercial ask simple for Acme: they want operational certainty. If Marissa's $3M sub-cap + defense costs gets us across the line, I recommend we propose a limited economic make-whole (e.g., 12 months of fees in escrow or a $50k holdback) and a defined SLA credit that applies only if an IP claim triggers service disruption.

Please also confirm: does the proposed carve-out cover claims against models/customers running customer-trained models on Redwood infra? We should explicitly exclude customer-provided content from Redwood liability and require Acme to warrant they have rights to content they load into the service.

If Legal can add the customer-content exclusion and preserve our cure options, I'm comfortable presenting the revised redline to Acme as a commercial compromise.

— Karthik Iyer
Head of Growth | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmedynamics.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - MSA redline (IP indemnity carve-out)

Rachel / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed compromise. Acme's counsel reviewed Marissa's suggested language. We can broadly accept a limited, quantified sub-cap for third-party IP claims if the language: (i) explicitly excludes IP indemnity from the general liability cap in Section X, (ii) covers reasonable defense costs, and (iii) does not require Acme to waive injunctive relief.

Two items for final redline: 
1) Carve-out scope: the indemnity must apply to claims based on Redwood's service or Redwood-supplied models, and expressly exclude claims arising solely from Customer Content or Customer modifications.
2) Cap amount: Acme will accept the $3,000,000 per-claim sub-cap for damages but insists that defense and reimbursement of settlement amounts remain outside the cap (i.e., defense costs plus settlements are recoverable in addition to the $3M damage cap).

If Redwood can accept those two points, Acme will sign. Please send a clean redline and the DocuSign link.

Forwarded attachment: ExhibitA-orderform.pdf

Best,
Laura Chen
Senior Counsel | Acme Dynamics
